summary: Executed focused backend+frontend entitlement regression for platform-access boundaries, canonical permissions payloads, and guarded routing smoke.

critical.issue: Restricted user (scope1-only test account) could create Scope 3 monthly emission (HTTP 200), violating hard outer entitlement boundary.
CORS preflight on public endpoint returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin='*' instead of explicit trusted origin while credentials are enabled.

action_items: Fix Scope 3 creation guard path for restricted users so platform access cannot be bypassed by KPI/user logic.
Trace why public preflight returns wildcard ACAO and enforce explicit origin response for credentialed auth routes.
Apply Scope 3 platform boundary consistently on GET /api/emissions/{id} and DELETE /api/emissions/{id} (currently no explicit assert_ghg_scope_access in handlers).
Frontend: tighten useModuleAccess fallback (currently allows all on config fetch failure), as this weakens hard entitlement boundary intent.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/modules/emissions/router.py: create/update enforce scope guard, but get-by-id and delete handlers do not explicitly apply assert_ghg_scope_access; boundary should be uniform across GET/POST/PUT/DELETE.
frontend/src/hooks/useModuleAccess.js defaults to allow-all when permissions fetch fails or key missing; this is risky for strict platform-access enforcement.
seed_data_creation: Transient scope3 emission was unintentionally created during failing guard test and immediately deleted (record_id=756c6cef-a7f3-4039-bc0e-d5d37c76c584).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file added for this scope: 8 tests total (6 passed, 2 failed). Frontend authenticated smoke passed (/dashboard and /ghg/scope3 rendered, no blank route regression).
rca of the issue: Scope3 creation failure reproduces with restricted user credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. POST /api/emissions accepts scope3 payload and persists record, indicating entitlement boundary is not effectively enforced for this user path. CORS mismatch appears at external/public layer despite explicit backend CORS config in server.py, suggesting middleware/config drift at runtime or proxy-level header override.
